title: Father's stories about Joe Oliver working on the riverfront
summary: His father knew Joe Oliver, who lived on Fort Street c. 1915, worked on the riverfront for white employers who let him play weekends, and bought his first cornet that way.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: By the way, uh, did you ever know where Joe Oliver was from?

My daddy knew Joe Oliver very well. He used to always tell me about Joe Oliver, how he was, uh, he used to eat so much, and how he was bragging on how much coffee and things he could drink always more than anybody. And, uh, I remember one time that he told me he was staying on 4th Street. And that was about around 1915, because my daddy used to always talk to me about, because it looked like he thought I had an inclination for music, playing music, you see. And he was a guitar player, you see. And, uh, he used to tell me about Joe Oliver, how he could play and how he could, uh, hold a note and how he worked on the riverfront. That's what it was, you see. Joe Oliver worked on the riverfront and used to take his horn and go down. And then he'd never remember anything he told me about a place on a magazine, I believe it was Magazine Authority, these white people that Joe Oliver worked for. And that's how he brought his first, uh, what they call him, cornette in those days. And the white people used to let him go out on the weekends and play, but he had to come back to come to work that Monday morning, see. And, uh.
You say he worked on the riverfront, was he a longshoreman?
I said I think so at that time.
And he take his cornette down with him?

Well, maybe he did, but I know he did that, because you know guys had to find some kind of way of making money, because music was, you know, just like his job. You know, on the weekend you get like that. And then I remember he told me strictly about this place, and I think it was his magazine, it might have been 30 magazines, some people he worked for. And they would have, you know, saw that he had a job, and then let him go out and play, you know, to keep up with his home, you see. And that's, uh, that's where the story is, as far as I can remember. And then one time, I remember, like I said, he stayed on Fort Street. I don't know whether it was Fort out there by the, what they call Irish Channel 2, see, because Fort runs all the way out that way. Yeah.
Well, Joe Oliver was here in the city when he was a young boy then.
I wondered if he was from the country originally?
